findings.title: Authorization check only verifies direct user ownership, missing team/delegation credential support
findings.body: The `deleteCacheHandler` checks `userId: user.id` to verify credential ownership. However, credentials can belong to teams or be used via delegation. If a user is a team member with access to a team credential's calendar cache, they will be denied access with 'Credential not found or access denied'. The UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) shows the delete option based on `cacheUpdatedAt` presence without checking whether the current user can actually authorize the deletion, leading to a guaranteed error for non-directly-owned credentials.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query after success
findings.body: After successfully deleting cache, the `deleteCacheMutation` calls `onSuccess?.()` but does not invalidate the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` tRPC query. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` which explicitly invalidates queries in `onSettled`, the delete cache mutation leaves the UI showing stale `cacheUpdatedAt` data. The cache status label ('Last updated: ...') will remain visible until an unrelated refetch occurs, giving the user incorrect information that cache still exists.

findings.title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale for date formatting ignores user's locale preference
findings.body: The `Intl.DateTimeFormat` on line 89 hardcodes `'en-US'` as the locale. The component already uses `useLocale()` for translations, but the date formatting does not respect the user's actual locale. Users with non-US locales will see dates formatted in US style (MM/DD/YYYY) rather than their preferred format. The locale should be derived from the user's settings or at minimum use `undefined` to respect the browser's locale.

findings.title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly without checking if calendar cache feature is enabled
findings.body: The handler creates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and queries the database for cache statuses on every `connectedCalendars` call, regardless of whether the calendar cache feature is enabled for the user's organization. Other parts of the codebase use `CalendarCache.init(null)` which respects feature flags and returns a mock when disabled. This results in unnecessary database queries (`groupBy` on CalendarCache) for all users, even those who don't use calendar cache.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual SQL statement
findings.body: The auto-generated warning comment states 'Added the required column updatedAt to the CalendarCache table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' However, the actual SQL on line 9 uses `DEFAULT NOW()`, which does provide a default value and is safe for non-empty tables. The misleading warning could cause confusion during migration review or if someone considers reverting/modifying the migration.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId fields, potentially breaking callers
findings.body: The `UserWithCalendars` type was changed to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` entries. Any code outside this PR that constructs a `UserWithCalendars` object (e.g., in tests, other handlers, or platform consumers) will now fail type checking if it doesn't include these fields. The `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `user.ts` was updated, but other callers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` may not have been.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-specific and will fail on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...` which is the macOS/BSD sed syntax. On Linux (GNU sed), the correct syntax is `sed -i -E ...` without the empty string argument. Running this script on a Linux development machine will produce an error: 'sed: can't read : No such file or directory'. Since this is a developer utility script, it should either detect the OS or use a portable alternative.
